name: Variation, evolution, selective breeding and genetic engineering

terms.definition: Differences in the characteristics of individuals in a population, caused by genes, the environment or both.
terms.examiner: Most variation has both genetic and environmental causes.

terms.definition: A change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time through natural selection, which may result in the formation of a new species.
terms.examiner: Life began more than three billion years ago.

terms.definition: Individuals best suited to their environment are more likely to survive, breed and pass on their alleles.
terms.examiner: Mutation → variation → selection pressure → survival → breeding → alleles passed on.

terms.definition: Organisms so different that they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring.
Humans choosing parents with desired characteristics to breed together, over many generations.
terms.examiner: Inbreeding can increase disease and reduce variation.

terms.definition: Modifying the genome of an organism by introducing a gene from another organism to give a desired characteristic.
terms.examiner: Example: bacteria making human insulin; GM crops resistant to pests.

terms.definition: A plasmid or virus used to insert a gene into the required cells.
terms.examiner: Higher tier. The gene is cut out with enzymes.
